walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Presentation & Interpretation — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Presentation & Interpretation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Presentation & Interpretation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which average is most affected by extreme outliers?
options: mean
median
mode
range
2/5 — by adding numerators and denominators separately.
1/6 — by multiplying the denominators only.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
5/6 — find common denominators (3/6 + 2/6).

mcqs.q: If a data set has an extreme outlier, which average is most affected?
options: The median is most affected because the outlier shifts the middle.
The mean — because every value (including the outlier) contributes to it.
1/6 — by multiplying the denominators only.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
(x + 3)^2 equals 2x + 6.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
(x + 3)^2 equals x^2 + 9 because squaring distributes over addition.
